what: One motor and a 24:1 worm drive lift a platform through a spatial six-hinge linkage. Two chains have parallel hinge axes within each chain; the chains are perpendicular to each other. Their common platform moves vertically while remaining level. The adapted 144-piece design adds four clearance plates beneath the deck. Two orthogonal hinge chains constrain a platform to vertical translation. Compare measured height with the sine law and the 24:1 worm drive.
try: Choose Sarrus Lift in Examples; the program loads into Blocks automatically. Press Run after resetting to the saved 45° pose. The linkage moves to 20°, returns to 45°, moves to 70°, then returns home.
Compare motor A angles −600°, 0° and +600° with the platform height. The worm needs 24 input turns for one output turn. The input has no artificial angle wrap.
Use manual override only for small jogs around the saved position. Keep the linkage between 20° and 70°; reset before running the experiment again.
why: Each pair of 120 LDU links contributes the vertical projection of its length. With 0.4 mm per LDU, h = 96 sin φ mm. Relative to the saved 45° pose, Δh = 96[sin(45° + A/24) − sin 45°] mm. The perpendicular hinge chains cancel the lateral motion that a single planar chain would allow.
matters: This is spatial straight-line guidance without a physical sliding rail. The solver uses an unpowered equivalent platform constraint and relaxes one redundant elbow constraint; body positions still come from gravity, contacts and finite motor torque. This stabilizes a closed constraint loop without prescribing its motion.
question: Does turning motor A by +600° raise the platform by the same distance that −600° lowers it from the 45° pose?
answer: No. The linkage angles are 70° and 20°. The ideal changes are about +22.33 mm and −35.06 mm. Equal angular changes produce unequal vertical travel because the sine function is nonlinear.
further: Compare this lift with Parallel Lift: one has spatial vertical guidance; the other follows a curved planar path.
The worm resists back-driving in this simulator. Compare that modeled behavior with active motor holding; it does not establish real friction, strength or lifting capacity.
Observe the platform angle as well as the motor encoder. A turning motor alone cannot establish that a closed linkage works.
formula: Δh = 96[sin(45° + A/24) − sin 45°] mm; 20° ≤ φ ≤ 70°. Four added clearance plates; 144 physical pieces.
